startup.name: Scheduling Wizard
startup.one_liner: Logistics infrastructure to modernize healthcare operations
startup.description: Washington DC team of 3 in Winter 2026 that does physician scheduling for hospital departments as a service, using its own scheduling programming language and AI workflows. It states 20 departments across 16 hospitals as clients and is expanding into patient triage and provider management.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent range). Up for real paying clients at 16 hospitals including well known academic centers, which is traction. Down for a three person service heavy team in a slow procurement field and healthcare IT competitors. Net about 4 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say that physician scheduling outsourcing looks like a service business with limited scale, and that incumbents QGenda and Amion own the category. Partners may also doubt that a three person team can scale to triage and provider management together, and may ask why hospitals would not simply buy software.

Time table Healthcare: seed p25 4, median 8.75, p75 27 months from batch start; series_a median 35. Healthcare IT tag 2018-2024: seed 50% (n=2).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 10.4 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchor 0.50 ever for Healthcare; Healthcare is slow to seed (median 8.75 months, p75 27) so only about 60 percent of eventual seeds close inside 10.4 months, giving 0.30, which is 0.6x of the anchor because of the window. Existing hospital clients are not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, the most common outcome for a small team that closes a first outside round quickly.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later YC median of 4.1M, with market pre money near 18M.
Strong seed led by a known fund, matching the upper quartile of 6.5M and above in press covered rounds.
Large hot category round; rare for a team this early.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if scheduling as a service looks like a consultancy, with revenue that scales by headcount and not by software, and if hospital procurement cycles slow new departments. Durate, Axle Health and Untether Labs sell similar scheduling software and raised little or nothing for years, and ReSchedule Med shut down. A three person team may take the YC deal and grow on revenue.

Axle Health took three years from batch to a 10M Series A and Bemlo stayed at a seed, so scheduling peers rarely raise an A this early even with hospital customers.

bands.rationale: Smaller later round near the 2022 and later p25 of 35M (n=9 only).
Typical Series C or later, 45M to 77M per the YC table and market monitor.
Breakout late round at unicorn scale; very rare in this cohort.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside ten months would need a category defining platform across health systems, as the largest hospital operations companies became only after many years. Qventus, a hospital operations YC peer from 2015, needed close to a decade, so the probability here is effectively zero.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stays a small, profitable service heavy business or sells to a scheduling or workforce vendor, the path of Bemlo and Untether Labs. Upside depends on turning the scheduling language into software that departments buy directly, against entrenched incumbents with thousands of hospital customers.

killers.mitigation: Win departments the incumbents serve poorly.

competition_now.name: QGenda
competition_now.what: Enterprise physician scheduling with AI optimization

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling is a constraint problem with hospital rules, and a domain specific language is a reasonable approach. A small team can build a solver in months, but EHR integrations and change management are the hard part, and rules coverage across departments is the moat.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents already have AI optimization features and customers, and Epic could add scheduling, but outsourced scheduling labour is not a target for them.

evidence.claim: KLAS tracks automated physician scheduling vendors and enterprise wide deployment is growing.
Incumbents claim thousands of hospitals, proving spend on scheduling.

actions: Track renewal and expansion across the 20 departments
roadmap.proof: Renewal above 90 percent with added departments.

actions: Automate the most common scheduling rules
roadmap.proof: Gross margin above 70 percent with schedulers per client falling.

pros.evidence: The company lists Mass General, Johns Hopkins, UT Southwestern and UCSF as clients across 16 hospitals.
Incumbents serve thousands of hospitals for scheduling.

brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Scheduling Wizard" --era 2022+: length bucket 12+, 4 or more syllables, alive 94.7 percent in bucket, no signal.
brand.rationale: A descriptive name states the product clearly like Instawork, but is generic and hard to trademark, and wizard may sound light for hospital procurement. Brand is secondary to renewal data.

narrative.headline: A three person scheduling service already inside 16 hospitals: seed is held to about 30 percent mainly by the 10 month window and slow healthcare timing, later rounds are near zero.
narrative.general_summary: Scheduling Wizard schedules physicians for hospital departments with its own scheduling language and AI workflows, and states 20 departments at 16 hospitals as clients. The window is 10.4 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17, short for healthcare where the median seed comes near 9 months and the p75 near 27, so seed is 0.30 against a Healthcare anchor of 0.50 for ever. Series A given seed is 0.04 in the window. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05 using only the input.
Seed means above about 1M from outside investors inside the 10.4 month window.
Client counts are company stated and not verified.
